source.title: MATE: Meet At The Embedding - Connecting Images with Long Texts
source.authors: Young Kyun Jang; Junmo Kang; Yong Jae Lee; Donghyun Kim

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some figure text and appendix text are OCR-garbled, but this does not appear to omit the study’s main sections.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies the Mutual-KNN and CKNNA alignment measures cited as proposed in the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, to a new set of model scales and datasets.
record.gate_note: The relevant result is the embedding-alignment analysis in Figure 3. Retrieval-performance tables and the MATE ablations are not rows: they report retrieval performance or method components, not alignment between representations.
record.test_reason: Section 4.4 applies the Platonic Representation Hypothesis measures (Mutual-KNN, CKNNA) to three CLIP image encoders. It compares each against an independently trained LLM text embedder (E5-Mistral) on paired COCO and DOCCI image-caption data. This bears on V1 and V2 for vision-to-LLM alignment, and on V6 through the two datasets. The analysis is small and was run to choose an encoder.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report three observations: larger encoders give higher alignment, lengthy captions give higher scores, and VLM-image-to-LLM alignment generally exceeds VLM-image-to-VLM-text alignment, dominantly for DOCCI. From these they hypothesize that the LLM shares more common representations with the larger image encoder, and they pick ViT-G. This is an encoder-selection analysis; the paper's main conclusion concerns MATE's retrieval performance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Mutual-KNN and CKNNA, measures used in the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, on CLIP image-encoder variants paired with LLM text embeddings and on COCO and DOCCI data.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment scores differ between the COCO short-caption and DOCCI lengthy-caption datasets. The paper reports results with both Mutual-KNN and CKNNA.

fits_no_version.finding: CLIP image embeddings align more with an independently trained LLM text embedder than with CLIP's own jointly trained text tower. The authors say this holds 'generally' and 'dominant' for lengthy DOCCI captions. Their image-to-own-text alignment also rises with encoder size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An independently trained stronger text model can align more closely with a vision encoder than that encoder's own contrastively co-trained text tower, especially on long text.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The scaling analysis includes only three CLIP image-encoder variants and keeps the LLM encoder fixed; it does not report an independent capability measure. Figure 3 is the sole source of the plotted alignment values, and the supplied figure text is too flattened to assign those values reliably. No uncertainty estimates or control comparisons are reported for this analysis.
record.rows_left_out: No other alignment results were reported for this claim. Retrieval results in Tables 2, 3, and 6 and the method ablation in Table 5 were omitted because they report retrieval performance or training-component effects rather than the alignment measure.

untested.parts: Only the vision side is scaled, across 3 CLIP encoders whose size is confounded with resolution, pre-training data and embedding dimension. The LLM is fixed. There is no capability measure and no other architectures or objectives.
The language model is not varied, so 'as both models get better' is untested. Vision capability is not measured.
Neighbour count and other similarity measures (e.g. CKA, SVCCA) are not varied; no out-of-distribution inputs. Only two kNN-based measures and two datasets are used.
Not tested as alignment. MATE's trained projection is assessed only by retrieval performance of the authors' own method, with no comparison to a native representation.
Not tested. Absolute scores are low (~0.11-0.36), but the authors do not discuss a ceiling or other causes.

missing.what: Partially legible numeric values from Figure 3. DOCCI Mutual-KNN values are 0.227, 0.234, 0.271, 0.275, 0.280, 0.301; DOCCI CKNNA values are 0.270, 0.277, 0.324, 0.329, 0.332, 0.360. COCO values are roughly 0.11-0.19. The rows record only 'figure only'.

record.verdict_notes: The VV rows were relinked to none because CLIP's image and text towers are trained jointly to align. The evidence for V1/V2 is therefore the VL rows only. 'Size' is confounded: ViT-L-336 is the same size as ViT-L with higher resolution, and ViT-G also has 5x the pre-training data. There is no uncertainty or control. The retrieval tables and the ablation (incl. Table 5 d,e image-encoder choice) report the authors' method performance and are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: The study varies CLIP image-encoder size while using a fixed LLM encoder. It does not test convergence across different architectures, objectives, training data, or modalities broadly, nor does it establish that model capability increases alongside size.
The study measures image-to-text alignment for paired data while varying the image encoder. It does not scale both the vision and language models or measure whether both become more capable.
The study compares two alignment measures and two datasets, but does not test changes to settings such as neighbour count or evaluate out-of-distribution inputs.

rows.subject: CLIP image encoders: ViT-L, ViT-L-336, ViT-G (reported size trend)
rows.operation_detail: Measured image-text embedding alignment across three CLIP image-encoder variants.
rows.note: The authors state that larger encoder sizes yield higher alignment scores. The plotted values are not reliably assignable from the flattened figure text.
rows.check: Measures a CLIP image tower against its own jointly trained text tower. That alignment is produced on purpose by the contrastive objective, so these are not independently trained models as V1/V2 require. The size trend is reported only in the authors' words; plotted values are not assignable.

rows.note: The authors state that larger encoder sizes yield higher alignment scores. They also say image-to-LLM alignment generally exceeds image-to-VLM-text alignment, with an exception allowed by “generally.”
rows.check: Trend rests on the authors' statement; COCO figure values (~0.11-0.19) cannot be reliably assigned to bars. Only 3 encoders. ViT-L vs ViT-L-336 differ in resolution, not size (300M vs 303M). ViT-G also differs in pre-training data (2B vs 400M) and embedding dimension, so size is confounded.

relationships.reason: Authors report larger encoders yield higher image-to-LLM alignment on both measures and datasets (F3-COCO-MK-VL, F3-COCO-CK-VL, F3-DOCCI-MK-VL, F3-DOCCI-CK-VL). Only 3 confounded models; figure-only.
